newsitem.title: GREECE: THOUSANDS OF GREEKS MARCH AGAINST AUSTERITY.
newsitem.headline: THOUSANDS OF GREEKS MARCH AGAINST AUSTERITY.

text.p: Thousands of teachers, students and construction workers marched through the streets of Athens on Wednesday protesting against the socialist government's tight incomes police and demanding higher salaries.

The march, by some 10,000 people, caused traffic chaos in the narrow streets of the capital for about three hours with stranded drivers blaring their horns and police blocking major streets for the march to pass through.

Minor clashes took place between teachers and police who used their batons to stop the protesters from reaching the Maximou Mansion housing the prime minister's office. There were no injuries or arrests.
High school and elementary school teachers have been on strike for 10 days and half the schools nationwide have been shut.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis, who also faces a farmers' revolt in central Greece, has drawn up a tight budget fr 1997 aiming to bring the country closer to its Europan Union partners.
He has weathered a series of protests since winning elections last September and has said he would not bow to economic demands by any particular group.
